examples.en: We sat around the stove and ate sweet potatoes.
The cat is dozing by the heater.
On cold days I want to sit by the heater.
I hung the wet gloves near the heater.
Grandmother told us old stories by the stove.
Don't get too close to the heater.

explain: 바닷가, 길가, 강가처럼 '-가'가 붙어 '곁'을 나타내요. 소리 때문에 사이시옷이 들어가서 '난로가'가 아니라 '난롯가'라고 써요.

phrases.en: It was cold, so I sat by the stove and warmed up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 난로 옆에 자리를 잡는 가장 흔한 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use: taking a seat beside the stove.

phrases.en: Grandmother knits by the stove.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에서'를 붙여 그 자리에서 하는 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the particle '에서' it marks an action done at that spot.

phrases.en: On the cold night, the family gathered by the stove.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-로'를 붙여 난로 쪽으로 모이는 방향을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-로' shows the direction of gathering toward the stove.

explain_en: Like 바닷가, 길가 and 강가, the '-가' ending means the area beside something. A 사이시옷 is added, so it is written '난롯가', not '난로가'.

en: the dog days of summer; sweltering midsummer heat

examples.en: This year's midsummer heat is really hard to bear.
Many people eat samgyetang during the dog days of summer.
The dog days have passed and the cool autumn has arrived.

examples.ko: 복더위 때문에 밤에도 잠을 잘 못 자요.
examples.en: Because of the midsummer heat, I can't sleep well even at night.

examples.ko: 이 복더위에 밖에서 일하시는 분들이 걱정돼요.
examples.en: I worry about the people working outside in this scorching heat.

examples.ko: 복더위가 끝나면 가족과 바다에 가고 싶어요.
examples.en: When the worst of the summer heat is over, I want to go to the sea with my family.

explain: 초복부터 말복까지, 삼복 동안의 가장 심한 더위예요. '삼복더위'라고도 해요. '폭염'은 기온이 높은 날씨 자체를 말하지만, '복더위'는 삼복이라는 시기의 더위를 가리켜요.

phrases.en: It's hard to go outside in the dog-day heat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻의 다른 말이에요. 초복, 중복, 말복의 더위를 모두 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Another word with the same meaning, covering the heat of all three dog days.

phrases.en: I eat watermelon to beat the midsummer heat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더위를 견딘다는 뜻으로 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation meaning to withstand the heat.

phrases.en: The midsummer heat starts this week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더운 시기가 시작될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the hot season begins.

explain_en: It means the fiercest heat of the three bok days, from chobok to malbok. It is also called '삼복더위'. '폭염' describes extremely hot weather itself, while '복더위' refers to the heat of that particular period.

examples.en: I saw beautiful coral under the sea.
The water is clear in seas where coral lives.
This necklace is made of red coral.
Warm seas have coral forests.
When the sea gets too warm, coral turns white.
Lots of fish gather near coral reefs.

explain: 식물이나 바위처럼 보이지만 산호는 동물이에요. 여러 산호가 모여 만든 바위 같은 지형은 '산호초'라고 해요. 붉은 산호는 장신구로도 써요.

phrases.en: Australia has a very large coral reef.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산호가 많이 모여 만든 바위 같은 지형을 뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A rock-like formation made by many corals together.

phrases.en: That shop sells red coral.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색으로 구분할 때 쓰고, 장신구 재료로 유명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to distinguish by color and known as a material for jewelry.

phrases.en: My mother received a coral necklace as a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산호로 만든 장신구를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to jewelry made from coral.

explain_en: Coral looks like a plant or rock, but it is an animal. The rock-like structure formed by many corals is called '산호초' (coral reef). Red coral is also used for jewelry.

en: to weed out; to thin out

examples.en: My mother thins out the lettuce in the garden.

examples.ko: 싹이 너무 빽빽해서 솎아 줘야 해요.
examples.en: The sprouts are too dense, so we have to thin them out.

examples.ko: 당근을 솎아 내면 남은 것이 더 크게 자라요.
examples.en: If you thin out the carrots, the remaining ones grow bigger.
My father is thinning the fruit on the apple tree.
I made kimchi with the thinned young radish.
When the seedlings grow, thin out the weak ones first.

explain: 그냥 '뽑다'와 달리 남은 것이 잘 자라도록 빽빽한 것 중 일부만 뽑을 때 써요. 상추, 열무, 과일 열매 이야기에 많이 나오고 '솎아 내다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I thinned out the weak sprouts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빽빽한 것 중 일부를 뽑아서 없앤다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means pulling out some of a crowded group to remove them.

phrases.en: I thinned the young radishes this morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 채소가 자라는 밭에서 하는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for work done in a field where vegetables are growing.

phrases.en: I made kimchi with the thinned young radishes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '솎다'를 명사 앞에 쓰는 활용형으로, 솎아 낸 어린 채소를 요리할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form before a noun, often used for cooking the young vegetables that were thinned out.

explain_en: Unlike plain '뽑다', it is for pulling out only some of a crowded batch so the remaining ones grow well. It is common with lettuce, young radish and fruit on trees, and you can also say '솎아 내다'.

examples.ko: 이 스프레이는 인화성이 높으니 불 근처에서 쓰지 마세요.
examples.en: This spray is highly flammable, so don't use it near fire.
Flammable materials have to be stored separately.
The box says to beware of flammability.
It is a highly flammable chemical, so I handle it carefully.

examples.ko: 인화성 액체를 차 안에 두면 위험해요.
examples.en: It is dangerous to leave flammable liquids inside a car.

examples.ko: 라이터 가스는 인화성이 있어서 열이 있는 곳에 두면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Lighter gas is flammable, so you shouldn't leave it near heat.

explain: '인화성이 높다/강하다'처럼 정도와 함께 쓰고, '인화성 물질'처럼 경고문에 붙여 써요. 반대로 불이 잘 붙지 않는 성질은 '불연성'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Keep flammable materials away from fire.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경고문과 안전 안내에서 가장 자주 보는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation in warnings and safety notices.

phrases.example: 이 약품은 인화성이 높아서 조심해야 해요.
phrases.en: This chemical is highly flammable, so be careful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불이 얼마나 잘 붙는지 정도를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe how easily something catches fire.

phrases.en: Gasoline is very flammable.
phrases.nuance_ko: '높다'와 거의 같은 뜻이고 성질이 세다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 높다, with a sense of the property being strong.

explain_en: It is used with degree words, as in '인화성이 높다/강하다', and attached to nouns on warnings, as in '인화성 물질'. The opposite, a quality of not catching fire easily, is called '불연성'.

examples.en: People in this village drink groundwater.
When it rains a lot, the groundwater increases.
We pumped up groundwater and watered the field.
Groundwater is cold even in summer.
The groundwater got dirty because of the factory.
This well is filled by groundwater.

explain: 땅 위를 흐르는 물은 '강물', 땅속에 있는 물은 '지하수'예요. '지하수를 파다', '지하수를 퍼 올리다'처럼 우물이나 펌프와 같이 많이 나와요. 마시는 물로는 '수돗물', '생수'와 비교해서 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: We dug for groundwater in the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우물을 만들 때처럼 땅을 파서 물을 찾는 일이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Digging into the ground to reach water, as when making a well.

phrases.en: We pump groundwater up with a pump.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅속 물을 위로 끌어올릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when drawing underground water up to the surface.

phrases.en: Groundwater increased after the rainy season.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅속 물의 양이 많아질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the amount of underground water increases.

explain_en: Water flowing above ground is 강물 (river water), and water under the ground is 지하수. It is often used with wells and pumps, as in '지하수를 파다' and '지하수를 퍼 올리다', and compared with 수돗물 (tap water) and 생수 (bottled water).

examples.en: Fruit flies are flying around the fruit.
In summer, lots of fruit flies show up in the kitchen.

examples.ko: 초파리를 쫓으려고 식초를 컵에 담아 뒀어요.
examples.en: I put vinegar in a cup to get rid of the fruit flies.
Because of the fruit flies, I put the fruit in the fridge.
Fruit flies are very small.

examples.ko: 과일 주변에 초파리 몇 마리가 맴돌아요.
examples.en: A few fruit flies are hovering around the fruit.

explain: 과일이나 음식물 쓰레기 주변에 모이는 아주 작은 파리예요. 보통 파리나 모기와 달라서 따로 '초파리'라고 불러요. 과학 실험에도 쓰이는 곤충으로 알려져 있어요.

phrases.en: If you leave fruit out, fruit flies gather.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌레가 모여드는 모습을 말할 때 '꼬이다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '꼬이다' describes bugs swarming to something.

phrases.en: I caught fruit flies by putting vinegar in a cup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에서 초파리를 없애는 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common when talking about getting rid of them at home.

phrases.example: 음식물 쓰레기 옆에 초파리 떼가 있었어요.
phrases.en: There was a swarm of fruit flies next to the food waste.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 마리가 모여 있을 때 '떼'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '떼' when many are gathered together.

explain_en: It is a very small fly that gathers around fruit and food waste. It is different from the ordinary housefly and the mosquito, so it has its own name. It is also known as an insect used in science experiments.
